/data/api_link	https://api.artic.edu/api/v1/artworks/31955
/data/title	Goblet (jia)
/data/date_display	Late Shang dynasty, 13th century–1046 B.C.
/data/description	Monumental scale and the precise casting of animal imagery distinguish this vessel as a commission of late Shang royalty. Two tiers of monster masks encircle the flared bowl. Elongated version of these masks, which may also be interpreted as paired serpents, descend the sharply tapered legs. A bovine head with sculpted horns crowns the strap handle. Pieces of the clay core, visible through holes in the legs, remain from the piece-mold casting process.
/data/short_description	The monumental scale and precise casting of animal imagery distinguish this vessel as a commission of late Shang royalty. Two tiers of monster masks encircle the flared bowl, while elongated versions of these masks, which may also be interpreted as paired serpents, descend the sharply tapered legs. A bovine head with sculpted horns crowns the strap handle.
/data/medium_display	Bronze
/data/provenance_text	Parish-Watson and Company, New York, 1922; sold to Kate Sturges Buckingham (1858–1937), Chicago[Kate served as executor of her sister Lucy Maud Buckingham's estate and continued expanding Lucy's collection following her death in 1920] Dec. 15, 1926; given to the Art Institute of Chicago, Dec. 15, 1926.
